paper_metadata.title: Efficient Evaluation of Exponential and Gaussian Functions on a Quantum Computer

experiments.description: Basic quantum exponentiation algorithm for evaluating exp(-alpha x') over a discretized domain using a sequence of controlled multiplications with overwriting multiplication routines.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Domain x' is discretized into 2^d uniformly spaced grid points encoded in d qubits; function values are stored in an n-qubit fixed-point register.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Compute f(x') = exp(-alpha x') on a discrete grid.

problem_instance.description: Generic discretized exponential-function evaluation; no single benchmark dataset.
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Transform x' to x = (x' - x'_min)/Delta so grid points become integers 0..2^d-1.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Analytical resource analysis; no numerical sampling or experimental runs reported.

quantum_resources.num_qubits: dn + n + d (excluding ancilla for multiplication)

speedup_claims.factor: dramatically reduced gate complexity relative to general-function polynomial evaluation methods
speedup_claims.baseline_method: Hänner et al. general function evaluator
speedup_claims.conditions: for exponential-function evaluation on discretized domains; basic algorithm uses d controlled multiplications
speedup_claims.caveats: No direct numerical baseline for exp_1 alone; detailed comparison appears later in Table II.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(n^log2(3) d) gate complexity with Karatsuba multiplication; O(nd) space with Gidney multiplication
complexity_analysis.total_operations_quantum: d multiplications in the basic algorithm

experiments.description: Refined gate-saving exponentiation algorithm for exp(-alpha x') using transformed constants Ai and reduced multiplication count m, including the second-half zeroing circuit when m < d.

algorithm.variant: gate-saving refined exponentiation with controlled OR/SWAP cleanup

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Same discretized domain as exp_1; only one n-qubit register for Ai is stored at a time and updated between multiplications.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Compute exp(-alpha x') with reduced multiplication count and cleanup for x >= 2^m.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: If any xi>=m = 1, output is zeroed using OR-gate chain and controlled SWAP; otherwise output remains Cm.
problem_formulation.num_ancilla_qubits: Up to d - m - 1 OR ancillas; additional n-qubit clean register for m < d in the non-overwriting implementation context

problem_instance.description: NISQ-oriented example with d = 7, n = 21, A = 0.389; also discussed for d = 8, n = 32.
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Binary expansion of constants Ai; only qubits differing between successive Ai values are flipped by X tensor p transformations.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Analytical resource estimates and a worked circuit example; no stochastic runs.

quantum_resources.num_qubits: 2n + d for overwriting multiplications; 49 qubits for the d=7, n=21 example (excluding multiplication ancillas)

results.value: m controlled multiplications plus optional OR/SWAP cleanup
O(log n) multiplications for fixed A

speedup_claims.factor: reduction from d multiplications to m multiplications
speedup_claims.conditions: when m < d; for fixed A and sufficiently large n, m = O(log n)
speedup_claims.caveats: Additional OR/SWAP cleanup is needed when m < d.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Gate complexity reduced to m multiplications, with m = O(log n) for fixed A; additional O(d) OR/SWAP cleanup when m < d
complexity_analysis.total_operations_quantum: m controlled multiplications plus optional OR/SWAP cleanup

experiments.description: Space-saving alternative exponentiation algorithm that uncomputes intermediate products to reduce qubit count, using non-overwriting controlled multiplication and wave-based register reuse.

hyperparameters.register_count_r: chosen such that r(r-1)/2 < m <= r(r+1)/2
hyperparameters.l_definition: largest integer satisfying l(l+1)/2 <= r(r+1)/2 - m

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Same discretized exponential evaluation as exp_1/exp_2, but intermediate registers are uncomputed and reused.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Compute exp(-alpha x') with reduced qubit footprint.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Same zeroing logic as the refined method when m < d; uses a clean ancilla register for final SWAP when needed.
problem_formulation.num_ancilla_qubits: Reduced via register reuse; additional OR ancillas may still be needed

problem_instance.description: NISQ-oriented example with d = 7, n = 21; table of m values up to 36; example wave structure shown for m = 4, 5, 6 with r = 3.
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Intermediate products are uncomputed to restore clean registers for reuse.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Analytical resource estimates; Table I enumerates r, mun, and total actual multiplications for m <= 36.

quantum_resources.num_qubits: rn + d for m = d; otherwise rn + 2d - m - 1 or (r + 1)n + 2d - m - 1 depending on equality case

results.value: less than double the gate-saving algorithm

speedup_claims.factor: space reduced from O(mn) to O(m^1/2 n)
speedup_claims.baseline_method: non-overwriting controlled multiplication without register reuse
speedup_claims.caveats: Gate cost increases, but is claimed to be less than double the gate-saving algorithm.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Space reduced from O(mn) to O(m^1/2 n); gate cost less than double the gate-saving algorithm
complexity_analysis.total_operations_quantum: mss controlled multiplications plus uncompute multiplications

experiments.description: Gate-count comparison experiment for exponential-function evaluation against the Häner et al. method, using the paper's gate-saving and space-saving implementations for two domain intervals and two target accuracies.

algorithm.variant: resource comparison against Häner polynomial-subdomain evaluator

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Same discretized exponential evaluation as above; comparison is against a general-function polynomial approximation method.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Evaluate exp(-x') with minimal Toffoli count and qubit count.

problem_instance.description: Exponential function benchmark with x'_min = 0 and alpha = 1, compared across two domain intervals and two accuracy thresholds.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Analytical Toffoli/qubit accounting; Table II reports minimal counts across configurations and compares to Häner's reported counts.

quantum_resources.num_qubits: Reported table values: 154, 134, 264, 233, 91, 71, 136, 105 for the paper's methods; Häner values also listed in Table II

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Choose n from target accuracy; choose d to minimize Toffoli count; compute m from A and n.

speedup_claims.conditions: exponential function, 10^-7 accuracy, 0 <= x' < 100, best-case parameters for each method
speedup_claims.caveats: Comparison is based on Table II and the paper's chosen best-case configurations.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Reported minimal Toffoli counts: 1620, 912, 4438, 2828 for gate-saving; 2308, 1409, 7531, 4278 for space-saving, depending on interval and accuracy.
complexity_analysis.total_operations_quantum: Controlled-multiplication-based evaluation with Toffoli counts reported in Table II

experiments.description: Gaussian-function evaluation exp(-alpha x'^2) using the same quantum exponentiation machinery plus an extra squaring step, with resource comparison against Häner et al.

algorithm.variant: Gaussian evaluation via exponentiation plus squaring

hyperparameters.symmetry_reduction: domain symmetry reduces d by one bit relative to naive doubling

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Domain is discretized as for the exponential case; an additional multiplication computes x^2 before exponentiation.

problem_instance.description: Gaussian benchmark with x'_min = 0 and alpha = 1, evaluated for the same two domain intervals and two accuracy thresholds as the exponential case.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Analytical Toffoli/qubit accounting; Table II reports minimal counts across configurations and compares to Häner's reported counts.

quantum_resources.num_qubits: Reported table values: 325, 141, 465, 262, 133, 93, 165, 142 for the paper's methods; Häner values also listed in Table II

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Choose n from target accuracy; choose d approximately doubled relative to exponential case, with symmetry reduction; compute m from A and n.

speedup_claims.conditions: Gaussian function, 10^-7 accuracy, 0 <= x' < 100, best-case parameters for each method
speedup_claims.caveats: Comparison is based on Table II and the paper's chosen best-case configurations.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Reported minimal Toffoli counts: 4468, 704, 8300, 3232 for gate-saving; 7546, 962, 14479, 5018 for space-saving, depending on interval and accuracy.
complexity_analysis.total_operations_quantum: Gaussian evaluation requires one extra multiplication for x^2 plus the exponential evaluation
